newsitem.title: DUBAI: APICORP eyes stake in Yanbu MTBE plant - MEES.
newsitem.headline: APICORP eyes stake in Yanbu MTBE plant - MEES.

text.p: The Arab Petroleum Investments Corp (APICORP) has indicated an interest in acquiring a 10 percent equity stake in Tahseen, the company that will run a planned MTBE plant at Yanbu, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) said on Monday.

"MEES understands that Alujain Corporation has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Arab Petroleum Investments Corporation in which the OAPEC-owned company has indicated an interest in acquiring a 10 percent equity stake in Tahseen..." the newsletter said.

The 850,000 tonnes a year plant, which Saudi Arabian firm Alujain will build in Yanbu on the kingdom's west coast to produce the environmentally-friendly fuel additive methyul tertiary butyl ether (MTBE), is due to come on stream in 1999.
Alujain officials said they have entered the final stages of negotiations with the three construction firms which have bid for the lumpsum turnkey construction contract on the project, MEES reported.
They are ABB Lummus Global Inc, a U.S. affiliate of Switzerland's ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG, Stone & Webster and Snamprogetti, a unit of the Italian energy giant ENI, it said.

"The discussions should be completed by the middle of April, after which project manager Bechtel is expected to submit its final contractor recommendation. This is now anticipated in mid-May. An award on the contract would be forthcoming shortly thereafter," MEES said.
Finnish energy group Neste Oy had signed a memorandum of understanding with Alujain to become a minority shareholder in the company operating the plant.

APICORP, based in the eastern Saudi city of al-Khobar, is an affiliate of the Organisation of Arab Petroleum Exporting Countries (OAPEC). It is owned by Iraq, Libya, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Syria, Qatar, Egypt, Bahrain and Algeria.
It finances oil and petrochemical trade and projects involving Arab states.
